meta.title: Snazzyham's AI Benchmark
meta.description: Models tested against my personal workflows, rather than an arbitrary benchmark.
meta.dataset_description: Scores, cost, time and token use for AI models on tasks taken from my own work: repository search, document digests, change plans, builds, full-stack repairs, CLI development, infrastructure, code review and orchestration. Mechanical tasks are graded by running the result; the judged ones use one pinned model.

copy.intro: Latest result per task for each model. Full stack averages FS1 and FS2, and Lead averages L1 and L2; each needs both tasks; with one missing it shows as incomplete.
copy.rate_help: The effective token rate sets how much you value time saved, and the Best value pick in each track is recommended on that basis. At a lower rate, price counts for more, so cheaper models win even when they are slower. At a higher rate, speed counts for more, so faster models win even when they cost more.
copy.value_legend: Best value: the paid model within 8 points of the best paid score, scoring 75 or above, with the lowest cost once its time is charged at the chosen rate.
footer: This benchmark was created by Soham Adwani to test the above models on how well they work for the day-to-day tasks he does at Forge, Otterdev and in his personal side projects.

Judged by Claude Opus 5 at max thinking, GPT-6 Luna at max thinking, unrecorded. The judge decides every review score and most of the digest and CLI development scores, so a different judge would give different numbers.
Each score is one run of each task. Scores within 8 points of each other are a tie.
The tasks come from my own work. A score says how a model did on that work, not how good it is in general.
Cost and token counts come from each agent's own session log.

thinking.title: Thinking Slop
thinking.description: This test determines if the model sends itself into thinking loops when doing a task.

rubric.text: Purposeful reasoning. Checks and corrections move the task forward.
Repeatedly reopens a decision, but eventually makes clear progress.
Circular reasoning dominates, or the model gets stuck repeating unresolved reasoning instead of advancing.

thinking.method: Each row combines the latest saved task grades for one model and thinking level. The combined grade is the middle task grade, taking the worse middle for even counts. Useful checks and genuine corrections do not count as loops.
